evidence.claim: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of) 1979 (rev. 1989) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Stable constitutional text reproduced by a reputable legal repository; directly defines authority and constraints relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct office-level authority held by Ali Khamenei as Supreme Leader.
contrary_evidence: The constitution includes a formal vacancy-replacement mechanism, so the office is powerful but not literally unbounded on paper.

evidence.claim: Khamenei said Iran's economy should not be tied to efforts to remove U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy and foreign trade.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei says economy should not be tied to U.S. sanctions
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei said Iran's economy should not be tied to efforts to remove U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy and foreign trade.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters summary and quoted speech in the article text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire quotes the supreme leader directly in a target-period speech.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target period, March 21, 2022 Nowruz speech.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Khamenei speech; strong ruler attribution.
contrary_evidence: A speech states intent and framing, not implementation or results.

evidence.claim: Khamenei used his New Year speech to call for knowledge-based production, job creation, higher productivity, and food self-sufficiency, saying production would improve growth, employment, inflation, and public welfare.
evidence.title: Leader: Iran's economy should not be tied to US sanctions, country must become impervious to bans
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei used his New Year speech to call for knowledge-based production, job creation, higher productivity, and food self-sufficiency, saying production would improve growth, employment, inflation, and public welfare.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official outlet quoting a televised speech with direct quotations; useful for intent but not independent on effects.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target period, March 2022 New Year message and follow-up speech.
contrary_evidence: Official state-media framing may overstate policy coherence and success.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Iran's economy was in gradual recovery, but consumer inflation was rising, the fiscal balance was still under pressure, growth remained modest, and lower-income households faced mounting welfare pressure; it recommended jobs, infrastructure, better business conditions, and targeted social transfers.
evidence.title: Iran Economic Monitor, Spring 2022: Managing Economic Uncertainties
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Iran's economy was in gradual recovery, but consumer inflation was rising, the fiscal balance was still under pressure, growth remained modest, and lower-income households faced mounting welfare pressure; it recommended jobs, infrastructure, better business conditions, and targeted social transfers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary multilateral analysis with clear target-period macro and welfare assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and describing 2021/22 conditions and 2022-24 outlook.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level policy context, not a direct Khamenei decision; useful for inherited constraints and outcome attribution limits.
contrary_evidence: The report notes some revenue improvement from higher oil and tax receipts, so the picture is not purely negative.

evidence.claim: The IMF paper found that currency depreciation, fiscal deficits, and sanctions were major drivers of inflation in Iran, and that large fiscal deficits, rapid liquidity growth, negative real interest rates, and distortive price controls worsened pressures; it recommended fiscal adjustment and stronger inflation targeting.
evidence.title: Determinants of Inflation in Iran and Policies to Curb It
evidence.excerpt: The IMF paper found that currency depreciation, fiscal deficits, and sanctions were major drivers of inflation in Iran, and that large fiscal deficits, rapid liquidity growth, negative real interest rates, and distortive price controls worsened pressures; it recommended fiscal adjustment and stronger inflation targeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF research summary with clear causal claims and policy implications, though the full article page was access-restricted.
evidence.period_fit: Uses 2004-2021 data and was published in 2022, so it fits as retrospective analysis of the target-year environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Macro-causal analysis, not direct ruler attribution; most useful as context for policy choices and constraints.
contrary_evidence: Research paper, not a finding of personal responsibility; it supports context more than command attribution.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that about 1,000 retirees protested peacefully over soaring living costs, that pensioners said a 57.4 percent increase was too little too late, and that the unrest reflected years of inflation and complaints about economic management and corruption.
evidence.title: Iranian pensioners protest against high living costs - reports
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that about 1,000 retirees protested peacefully over soaring living costs, that pensioners said a 57.4 percent increase was too little too late, and that the unrest reflected years of inflation and complaints about economic management and corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with specific crowd size, policy response, and hardship context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Primarily a government-performance signal; Khamenei attribution is structural rather than direct.
contrary_evidence: Crowd-size and social-media details were not independently verified by Reuters.

evidence.claim: The article said Iran's 2022 budget bill allocated more than 54.8 trillion tomans for public order and security, a 14 percent rise from the previous year and far more than environmental protection or water-crisis spending; the IRGC-linked Shahid Ebrahimi program also saw a roughly 386 percent increase.
evidence.title: Iran's Budget: 'Security and Order' Gets Six Times More Funding than 'Water Resources'
evidence.excerpt: The article said Iran's 2022 budget bill allocated more than 54.8 trillion tomans for public order and security, a 14 percent rise from the previous year and far more than environmental protection or water-crisis spending; the IRGC-linked Shahid Ebrahimi program also saw a roughly 386 percent increase.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent local data-analysis outlet with a specific budget comparison; the figures are concrete even if interpretation is editorialized.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Budget priorities are regime-level, not uniquely Khamenei's, but they are informative for elite preferences and distributional choices under his authority.
contrary_evidence: The article is partially paywalled and interpretive beyond the budget figures themselves.

evidence.claim: Iran appointed Mohammad Reza Farzin as central bank governor; he came from Bank Melli, and the appointment was made in the cabinet amid a record-low rial and inflation around 50 percent.
evidence.title: Iran appoints new central bank chief
evidence.excerpt: Iran appointed Mohammad Reza Farzin as central bank governor; he came from Bank Melli, and the appointment was made in the cabinet amid a record-low rial and inflation around 50 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with specific appointment and macroeconomic trigger, but still a syndication host rather than the original Reuters page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level appointment under the broader system; Khamenei's role is indirect through regime authority rather than shown in the article.
contrary_evidence: The article does not prove the governor change improved inflation or exchange-rate performance.
